text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000006 bills 99215 well above expected levels, much of it on low-complexity patients, but the few charts returned all support the billed level, too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward upcoding: the 99215 share is elevated in every complexity band from 0 to 4 conditions, and most 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry routine diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection, UTI, rash or follow-up (e.g., C0002229, C0002395, C0003125), which would rarely need high-complexity decision making. The documentation points the other way. All four documented 99215s, including C0003128, were recorded at high MDM, and the data-reviewed claims all had a lab or test line. But records came back for under 1% of claims, so this is too few to clear or implicate the provider. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the sampled 0–1 condition 99215 claims, starting with the acute-diagnosis visits listed above. When those charts arrive, check them for cloned or templated MDM language."}
